2944052904a3f1d170c46769c9c1fa5d7be23118.summary: Free decryptor page from Emsisoft, published 2016-12-23, for GlobeImposter ransomware. GlobeImposter is a copycat of the Globe ransomware kit that imitates its ransom notes and file extension. Encrypted files get a .crypt extension and keep their base name. Decryption needs a matching pair of an encrypted file and its unencrypted original. The tools may not work on all ransomware versions and are provided without warranty.

298101821b6b52ac6c12254de806b87efa15f260.summary: CSHARP-STREAMER is a modular .NET remote access trojan analysed by HiSolutions. The report says its casework saw the Metaencryptor ransomware group using it, and that RAT usage rose sharply in Q3 2023. Other public reports tie it to REvil and ALPHV deployments. The report suggests it may be sold as a service to ransomware groups, and it provides detection rules and identifying strings. Most attribution in the report is hedged.

hedges: The report assumes Metaencryptor has a special interest in IT service providers, based on its own visibility.
The report could not rule out that the malware is a malware-as-a-service product or that its modularity is meant to evade analysis.
The report says the reasoning behind the modular design is unclear.
The report is not confident that the Arista-described attack and its own case share one threat actor.
The report says the switch in TTPs suggests an initial access broker gave Metaencryptor access; this is an inference.
The report expects the malware is provided as a service to ransomware groups.
The report says the early samples are probably early development versions of the malware.
The report could not identify 2022 samples but is confident the malware was in use in that period.
